snippet.title: I Built an Agentic Software Factory with Codex and Claude Code
snippet.description:
🔗 Skills used in this video: https://aiengineer.co/start/

In this video I walk through how I build a software factory: an automated pipeline where agents pick up tickets, refine them, implement the change, run tests and reviews, and open a pull request without me sitting in the terminal.

I show this on a real open source project called Factory, written in Rust, which polls GitHub issues for labels, spawns an agent in an isolated Git worktree, and moves the work through triage, implementation, and review. It solves the problem of tedious mechanical work sitting in a backlog while you babysit agents one conversation at a time.

What you'll learn:
- What a software factory is and how it maps onto the development loop you already follow
- The task to PR workflow I use for most of my implementation work
- How a triage agent turns a vague ticket into an implementation ready spec
- How label based triggers move work through the pipeline automatically
- Worktree isolation vs Docker sandboxes, and why I am still working this out
- Scheduled workflows, including a bug finder that opens tickets on its own
- The honest limits: token cost at scale, and the fact that only a share of your tickets should ever be handed off this way

snippet.title: 3 Ways to Make Your First Money Online
snippet.description:
How to make your first money online: the 3 ways I have done myself. Buy and sell, an affiliate website, and selling before you own the stock.
Real numbers: old Fossil watches found at 15, sold for double or triple, maybe 1,000 or 2,000 euros made like this.

I explain, in simple words, three beginner ways to make money online that I have done myself, with the real numbers I had. It is for you if you want to start with a small budget (something around $20 to $50 max for your first item) and want a concrete, honest place to begin. Simple and practical: just what worked for me.

Chapters
00:00 3 ways to make your first money online
00:12 Way 1: buy and sell
00:47 Pick a niche: watches
01:07 Found at 15, a 1 euro battery
01:46 Sell for double or triple
01:57 No expert needed: ask Claude for prices
02:13 Buy in person, pay cash
02:36 How much per month
03:11 Way 2: affiliate website
03:27 Domain name, brand and logo with AI
03:51 SEO or faceless content
04:09 Free site with Vercel, code with Claude
04:34 Affiliate programs like Amazon
04:57 Way 3: sell before owning
05:23 Paid 20 euros, sold for 60
05:34 Sell first or buy stock
06:06 Next video: a buy and sell how-to
06:25 Where to start

Key takeaways
- Buy and sell is the easiest way to start: find something not very expensive, around $20 to $50 max, in one niche you get to know well. Mine was watches.
- Fossil watches cost around 100 or 200 in the shop. I found old ones at 15. 90% of the time, the sellers just don't know how to change the battery (about 1 euro). Clean them, use an old box, package well, take a good photo, then sell for double or triple.
- You do not need to be an expert: take a photo, ask Claude, and check prices everywhere to see if the price is good or very low.
- Go in person and pay cash: people often sell with a lower price. Then you package everything, sell online and just ship.
- Buy and sell can bring around 100 or more per month. My best months were around 500. It takes time, but 2 hours per day can already make good money.
- Affiliate website: a domain name for 10 to 20 dollars, a brand and a logo with AI, a free site on Vercel, code with Claude, then SEO or faceless content, then plug in affiliate programs like Amazon. It is not very fast, you don't have the control and it is a lot of technical stuff. But with $10, you can make money online.
- Sell before owning: buy cheap stock (AliExpress) and resell on Facebook Marketplace, eBay or other marketplaces. I paid like 20 euros for watches and sold them for 60. I have sold before buying, but it is better to buy a lot and have stock.

Next video: how to buy and sell on Leboncoin, eBay and other marketplaces, with everything I have done.
